research_responses.text:
I read it closely. My view of the campaign has changed a bit: **we should stop treating “more obstruction computations” as the default route to a CE.** The document leaves us with two fundamentally asymmetric candidates.

For \(D_{01}=K_0\#(-K_1)\), we already have the intended Abe–Tagami/Miyazaki non-ribbon side, subject to exact identification/hypothesis auditing; what is missing is an actual smooth slice disk in standard \(B^4\). For KDG, sliceness is the supplied side and global non-ribbonness is missing. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

The newest work also tells us what **not** to do. The tempting Donaldson trace-cap attack on \(D_{01}\) is dead because the actual double-branched trace contains an indefinite \(2H\) subspace. Importantly, that says nothing about whether \(D_{01}\) is slice. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

So here's how I think we actually hunt the CE now.

**First: finish the whisker gate, because we're one exact computation from resolving an entire proposed \(D_{01}\) construction.** Pass08 already reduced things to a finite set of \(SL(2,\mathbf F_5)\) possibilities, but those 12 surviving branches aren't probabilities or candidate maps—the physical product-disk map hasn't been identified. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"} We need the actual based map
\[
\phi:\pi_1(\text{lower exterior})\rightarrow\pi_1(\text{upper exterior}),
\]
including the whisker produced by the glued arcs. The label-preserving mirror correspondence has already eliminated most of the ambiguity; the paste says the whisker is now the missing datum. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}

There are two possible outcomes, and **both tell us what to do next**.

If a separating \(SL(2,5)\) representation genuinely extends over the disk exterior, that particular modifying annulus is obstructed. Don't widen the finite quotient search. Kill that construction, record why, and move on.

If the physical branch survives, don't celebrate yet. Immediately attempt to turn the existing genus-one twice-banded surface into an actual annulus by finding the missing **nonseparating compression disk**. The source itself identifies that as the next geometric obligation: compression curve, framing, complement disjointness, boundary identification, everything explicit. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

And this is where I would make the major strategic commitment:

\[
\boxed{\textbf{Try to construct sliceness of }D_{01},\textbf{ rather than infer it.}}
\]

Why? Because \(D_{01}\)'s missing half is existential. One explicit annulus \(K_0\sim K_1\) solves it. We can verify a proposed surface locally and globally. By contrast, KDG's missing half is universal: proving that **no ribbon disk exists** is inherently nastier, and several specialized Eisermann/satellite tests have already passed without resolving that question. The campaign instructions themselves prioritize turning the actual annulus-twist geometry into a surface movie or handle construction. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"}

If the current product-disk construction dies, I would **not** return to huge band enumeration. I'd attack the annulus twist itself. Start with the known \(K_0\to K_1\) trace and ask whether births/deaths allow its stabilized concordance to destabilize in a way the ribbon-only searches could never see. We're allowed a general smooth concordance:

\[
\chi=0,\qquad
\partial A=(-K_0)\sqcup K_1,
\]

with births, saddles and deaths. We do **not** need a ribbon concordance. That's exactly the distinction that makes this lane interesting. The original campaign instructions explicitly require tracking Euler characteristic, connectedness, framing, ambient manifold, and ensuring the result is an annulus in \(S^3\times I\), not merely a surface in some homotopy cobordism. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}

There's also a second constructive version worth retaining: find a known ribbon \(J\) for which
\[
D_{01}\#J
\]
has an explicit ribbon disk. Because \(J\) is slice, that would establish sliceness of \(D_{01}\) without asserting that \(D_{01}\) itself is ribbon. The document explicitly calls out this stabilization route. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"} That's a much more targeted search than arbitrary bands on \(D_{01}\).

KDG stays alive as the **secondary lane**. But I'd only pursue a proposed KDG invariant after proving that it is genuinely ribbon-specific—if it vanishes on every smoothly slice knot, it cannot distinguish our already-slice KDG from ribbon knots. That's exactly the filter the campaign document demands. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="8"}

So the CE hunt I want is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\textbf{NOW: } &&\text{derive whisker}\to\phi\to12\ SL(2,5)\text{ extension tests};\\
&\textbf{IF SURVIVES: }&&\text{construct the nonseparating compression disk}\to
K_0\sim K_1;\\
&\textbf{IF KILLED: }&&\text{direct annulus-twist movie / ribbon stabilization construction};\\
&\textbf{SECONDARY: }&&\text{KDG only when we have a genuinely ribbon-only global obstruction.}
\end{aligned}
\]

And the jackpot condition is wonderfully uncomplicated. If we ever produce an explicit smooth annulus \(K_0\sim K_1\) in **standard** \(S^3\times I\), then \(D_{01}\) is slice. At that moment we stop everything, independently reconstruct the disk, re-audit the Abe–Tagami/Miyazaki non-ribbon theorem and exact knot identification, and try as hard as possible to destroy our own result. Only if both sides survive do we write

\[
\boxed{\text{SLICE}+\text{NON-RIBBON}=\text{CE}.}
\]

We're not there. But unlike a week ago, I think we now have an actual **construction funnel** rather than twenty interesting invariants. That's where I'd put the effort. 🎗️🔬

This is a meaningful result, even though it killed our own idea rather than producing the CE. The important thing is that it seems to have killed it for a **structural reason**, not because a search happened to return nothing.

The core lemma is strong:

\[
Q_W\cong H,\qquad p:W_2\to W,\quad \deg p=2
\]

and, assuming the checked relative-fundamental-class argument,

\[
Q_{W_2}(p^*x,p^*y)=2Q_W(x,y).
\]

Since \(Q_W\) has signature \((1,1)\), its pullback already supplies both a positive and negative direction. Thus

\[
b_2^+(W_2)\ge1,\qquad b_2^-(W_2)\ge1.
\]

No handle slides remove that positive direction, and negative blow-ups certainly don't. So the proposed strategy of taking **this particular branched-cover trace and capping it to manufacture a negative-definite Donaldson setup is dead**. That's considerably better than spending another session trying increasingly elaborate Kirby moves on something algebraically impossible.

The corrections are important too. In particular,

\[
5^2=25\equiv-1\pmod{13}
\]

removes the orientation trick, while recognizing that sliceness of \(D_{01}\) would provide a rational-homology cobordism \(Y_0\to Y_1\), rather than a rational-ball filling of \(Y_1\), prevents the bogus \(\langle-1\rangle^7\) target from contaminating later arguments.

But the part I'm most interested in now is the **whisker**.

We've reduced what sounded like a messy diagram-identification problem to a very specific missing datum:

\[
\boxed{\text{explicit based lower}\to\text{upper map }\phi}
\]

with the unbased crossing correspondence apparently already canonical because `.mirror()` preserves the labels. The remaining job is therefore not “search for a map”; it's to compute the basepoint transport through the recorded glued arcs.

And then we get a genuinely crisp experiment:

\[
12\text{ surviving }SL(2,\mathbf F_5)\text{ boundary colourings}
\longrightarrow
\text{apply the correct based }\phi
\longrightarrow
\text{disk-exterior extension test}.
\]

If one representation separates **and genuinely extends over the disk exterior**, that kills the modifying annulus. If none does, that's a clean negative for this obstruction—not evidence of sliceness.

So I would absolutely do the stated next action and **nothing broader yet**: derive the whisker word symbolically from the cut endpoints, verify it by at least one independent path/composition consistency check, then rerun only those 12 survivors.

One subtlety I'd enforce before trusting the output: distinguish a change of basepoint/whisker, which should act by conjugation on the appropriate representation data, from an actual change in the induced peripheral automorphism. If two implementations of the whisker differ only by the expected inner automorphism, their extension verdict should agree. That gives us a very nice sanity check on the construction.

Current board, then:

\[
\boxed{\text{CE: NO}}
\]

Trace-plus-cap Donaldson route: **killed**.  
General \(D_{01}\) sliceness: **still completely open**.  
Based-map obstruction: **one explicit whisker computation away from being testable**.

That's where I'd put Astra next. 🔬🎗️ And I like that we're now killing our own attractive ideas when the topology says they're wrong—that's exactly what makes a positive result later believable.

Yeah. That’s a much less exciting end-of-day report than we wanted. 🥲 But I think the distinction in it is important.

We did **not** move substantially closer to a counterexample today in the sense of acquiring one of the two missing proofs. We moved closer to knowing which computations and arguments can actually be trusted.

And the board is now brutally simple:

\[
\boxed{D_{01}:\quad \text{non-ribbon}+\color{gray}{\text{ sliceness unknown}}}
\]

versus

\[
\boxed{K_{DG}:\quad \text{slice}+\color{gray}{\text{ non-ribbonness unknown}}}.
\]

That's why I agree with the proposed change in strategy. Another enormous short-band search is unlikely to answer either missing theorem. For \(D_{01}\), the question should become constructive:

\[
\text{annulus-twist geometry}
\longrightarrow
\text{explicit concordance/movie}
\longrightarrow
\text{verified smooth disk in }B^4.
\]

And crucially, we shouldn't require that construction to look ribbon. If we're trying to produce a **slice-but-not-ribbon** knot, restricting the search to ribbon-like movies is almost perversely restrictive. Births, deaths, and saddles are fair game; what ultimately matters is that the resulting properly embedded smooth surface in \(B^4\) is a disk.

That's the direction I'd start with next time.

But I also wouldn't interpret today as “we failed, therefore tomorrow we need to compensate by working harder.” We hit the usage limit you chose, and stopping there is sensible. The repo is in a better epistemic state than it was this morning: false exclusions were corrected, checkpoint/coverage logic was repaired, Eisermann was calibrated properly, the census was pushed through its finite range, and an expensive KDG obstruction was actually resolved rather than left hanging.

None of that is the CE. **CE remains NO.**

Tomorrow's objective doesn't need to be “find the counterexample tomorrow.” It can be much sharper:

> Determine whether the specific annulus-twist relation underlying \(D_{01}\) can be promoted to an explicit smooth concordance of the required topology.

If **yes**, then we audit the hell out of it, because we'd suddenly be extremely close.

If **no**, we want a precise obstruction explaining why that construction fails—not another 500,000 moves and a sad `0 hits` line.

For tonight, I'd leave the mines exactly where they are. 🎗️⛏️ We have a much better question waiting for the next session.

Yes, Scott—**I would give Opus a separate construction task: turn one actual mutation pair into an explicit smooth-concordance problem, while Astra continues the marked-axis and surgery geometry.** 🎗️

Two corrections matter. The reported “1,472 mutant pairs” are **candidate groups, not certified mutation pairs**, according to Research/45. Also, the universal claim that positive mutants are concordant is already false; the task must concern a particular pair and an actual construction.  :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

Keep two other distinctions intact: matching the paper’s Alexander polynomial does **not** close the paper-to-diagram transcription gap, and Astra’s explicit genus-one package supplies a definite surgery construction but not yet an identified nonribbon knot with a smooth slice disk.  :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"} The cable-stabilizer ribbon route should remain retired under its recorded theorem assumptions—not mistaken for an obstruction to every smooth slice construction. 

Give Opus this:

```text
Opus, continue the SR-Foxy Slice–Ribbon counterexample campaign.
This is a construction session, not another census report or general
assessment of whether the problem is difficult.

The objective is an explicitly identified knot K with BOTH:
(1) a smooth properly embedded disk in the standard B4;
(2) a valid proof that K is not ribbon.

No discovery is guaranteed. Nevertheless, an open construction problem
is the task to work on—not a reason to stop before attempting it.

You already know your completed searches. Incorporate the newer Astra
work below, then make a concrete attempt at the missing smooth geometry.

STARTING STATE AND COORDINATION

Work from the actual current main, incorporating work after 7585c92
safely. Preserve concurrent changes and running jobs. Do not create a
branch, reset, force-push, or overwrite another session’s artifacts.

M5 is finished as a bounded numerical search:
3486 records, 3477 numerical signature outcomes, 9 UNKNOWN, no matching
0-surgery signatures found by the authoritative merge. Preserve the
raw records and their hashes. Do not rerun that population or relabel
numerical nonmatches as certified nonhomeomorphisms.

The equal-volume filter did not target the mechanism needed. Do not
extend its crossing bound without a genuinely different construction.

Retain Corollary Q with its exact hypotheses and Theorem F/Sun
dependence. It strengthens an available nonribbon route; it does not
construct a concordance. Do not spend this session reproving it.

Astra is pursuing the marked-axis, genus-two/mixed-handle, and explicit
surgery-boundary geometry. Read its latest handoff and Research/44–49
only far enough to avoid duplication and import applicable corrections.

In particular:
- The fixed cable-stabilizer ribbon route has a recorded global
  exclusion, not merely a failed first band.
- The explicit genus-one correction is not the required annulus.
- Its actual surgery knot K_new remains distinct from a claimed D01
  identification until a geometric identification is supplied.
- Equality of words, E=0, and a matching Alexander polynomial do not
  identify an embedded endpoint or surgery knot.
- Matching the paper’s Alexander polynomial does not verify the
  paper-to-stored-link transcription.
- The stored knots may still be usable directly under a theorem whose
  hypotheses are independently certified; a paper label is not itself
  required for every nonribbon proof.

Your primary independent task is the concrete mutation/tangle route in
Research/45. Develop it beyond a literature suggestion.

1. SELECT AND CERTIFY ONE ACTUAL MUTATION PAIR

Treat the approximately 1472 reported groups as candidate groups, not
certified positive-mutant pairs.

Use the saved population to select a pair with a geometrically simple
potential Conway decomposition and a credible nonribbon certificate for
its difference knot. Favor accessible tangles and existing exact input
data over numerical closeness.

Recover the actual diagrams. Exhibit a sphere meeting the knot in four
points, with the inside and outside tangles explicitly marked. Specify
the mutation involution and its endpoint permutation. Perform the
rotation and identify the resulting diagram with the proposed partner.

Check the orientation compatibility required for positive mutation.
Do not infer mutation from equal volume, Alexander polynomial, or Floer
data. Do not assume full bigraded HFK is mutation invariant.

For this particular pair K and K*, establish:
- the knot identities and their distinctness;
- the exact hypotheses of the nonribbon theorem to be used on
  D = K # (-K*);
- the scope and trust assumptions of each certificate.

Do not use failure to find an isomorphism as an exact distinctness proof.
Do not treat two matching knot polynomials as a positive identification.

Use the existing minimality/Miyazaki machinery where it actually
applies. Prefer an already established route over a newly conditional
one when both suffice.

A qualifying pair does NOT need homeomorphic 0-surgeries. Remove that
unnecessary requirement from this concordance experiment.

If the first proposed pair is not actually mutant, or the difference
has no applicable nonribbon certificate, record the precise failure and
select another for a stated geometric reason. Do not turn this into
another broad invariant sweep.

2. ATTEMPT A RELATIVE TANGLE CONCORDANCE

Write the certified pair as closures of

    K  = U glued to T,
    K* = U glued to rho(T),

with the outside tangle U unchanged and every boundary identification
recorded.

Attempt to construct a smooth concordance, relative to the endpoints,
from T to a tangle S that is invariant under rho up to an explicitly
recorded compatible isotopy.

This gives a concrete proposed mechanism:

    T --C--> S --isotopy--> rho(S) --reverse(rho(C))--> rho(T).

Closing with the product concordance of U would then give a smooth
concordance from K to K*.

This is a construction target, not an existing certificate. Supply C,
the symmetry of S, and the endpoint-compatible gluing. Do not replace
any of them with an invariant match.

For a two-string tangle, track the two properly embedded rectangle
components of the relative concordance, including their side
boundaries. They must remain disjoint and have the correct endpoint
genealogy. Account for transient circles, births, saddles, and deaths;
do not hide extra genus or closed surface components.

Permit genuinely smooth concordances with maxima. A ribbon-only search
is not the whole problem, and a direct ribbon concordance between
distinct minimal knots is not the construction to request.

One possible design is a common successor:
construct T -> S and rho(T) -> S in the permitted direction, then
reverse one concordance. Check the direction against the minimality
theorems. Do not accidentally seek a common predecessor that those
theorems already exclude.

If C is only an isotopy and the symmetry then makes K and K* isotopic,
you have lost the required distinctness. Detect that immediately.

3. BUILD THE MOVIE FROM THE TANGLE’S ACTUAL STRUCTURE

Inspect the selected tangle for a specific geometric mechanism:
a local slice-string-link replacement, a cancellation involving
identified bands, or a controlled birth/saddle/death construction.

Choose the mechanism because of a visible feature of this tangle.
Do not enumerate arbitrary band moves on the whole difference knot.

For every proposed elementary move, save:
the input and output diagram, attaching intervals, routing,
orientations, and the reason the move contributes the claimed smooth
surface rather than an unrecorded crossing change.

A crossing change by itself gives a singular trace, not a concordance.
If using immersed intermediate surfaces, record every double point,
its two sheets, sign, whiskers, and relevant group label.

Opposite signed intersections are not automatically a Whitney pair.
Construct the Whitney circle, check its ambient group class and
framing, and account for the disk’s interior intersections. No automatic
smooth Whitney trick, unspecified clean disk, or invented dual sphere.

Use computation to test these concrete objects. Do not use a large
number of failed moves as a substitute for understanding the tangle.

The first substantial milestone should be an explicit relative movie
or a specific obstruction to a specified movie—not another statement
that concordance is unknown.

4. USE A FAILURE TO DESIGN THE NEXT CONSTRUCTION

If the attempt fails, identify the exact reason:
endpoint incompatibility, unavoidable genus, a nontrivial group class,
framing, interior intersections, an obstruction to concordance, or
collapse to an isotopic pair.

Then change the feature responsible. Do not repeat geometrically
equivalent attempts under different labels.

If the census examples have unsuitable tangles, reverse the design:
start with an explicit relative concordance to a symmetric tangle,
then seek an outside closure for which the two resulting knots are
distinct and satisfy an available nonribbon criterion.

Do not assume such a closure exists. Test its relevant structure
early. In particular, an easy local construction may force composite
or satellite knots, destroy the required fiberedness or irreducibility,
or make the two closures isotopic.

This construction-first search is allowed to leave the old census
population. The point is to select candidates by a prospective smooth
concordance mechanism, not by a volume coincidence.

Your M1/M2/M3 categories are a project map, not a theorem exhausting
every possible construction. A blocked family stays blocked; a
different mechanism should be judged on its actual hypotheses.

Likewise, Davis–Park–Ray must be applied to the families and statements
it actually treats, not converted into a universal prohibition on
satellite constructions.

5. USE LITERATURE TO ENABLE A PARTICULAR MOVE

Search primary sources when a specific relative-concordance,
mutation, string-link, or ribbon-obstruction theorem could change the
next construction.

Begin with Research/45’s source corrections. Positive mutation does
not preserve smooth concordance in general. The question here is
whether our specified pair admits a particular concordance.

For a useful theorem, write its exact hypotheses beside our actual
objects. Distinguish smooth from topological concordance, standard
ambient products from homology or homotopy cobordisms, and knot
concordance from weaker equivalence relations.

A theorem that supplies only a genus-positive cobordism or a homology
cobordism does not finish this route.

Do not spend the session assembling a bibliography. Use a source to
construct or reject a named move, then return to the geometry.

6. TAKE THE CONSTRUCTION THROUGH TO THE COUNTEREXAMPLE

If a concordance K -> K* is obtained, write out the construction of the
smooth slice disk for D = K # (-K*) in the standard B4. Verify the
orientations, boundary knot, embeddedness, and ambient manifold.

Apply the nonribbon proof to that SAME D. Check every hypothesis and
retain any genuine theorem or software dependence.

If the construction has changed either endpoint, redo the endpoint
identification before importing the old nonribbon certificate.

Do not stop at a promising movie prefix when the next move is concrete.
Continue through the complete certificate.

Do not call any of the following a counterexample:
a matching invariant package;
a concordance candidate;
a slice disk in an unidentified homotopy ball;
a ribbon-search failure;
or a disk for a different boundary knot.

7. USE ASTRA’S OUTPUT WITHOUT DUPLICATING ITS WORK

If Astra publishes an ordinary diagram of K_new while this session is
running, that creates a second concrete task for you: investigate
nonribbonness of that exact knot while Astra handles the slice geometry.

Do not reconstruct its mesh or restart its unlink-isotopy calculation.
Use the delivered diagram and surgery identification.

If the archive is not available to this session, do not pretend to
have its coordinates or diagrams. Request the exact missing artifact
only when needed; the independent tangle construction can proceed
without it.

Do not apply a fibered irreducible-Alexander theorem directly to a knot
merely because its polynomial is d(t)^2. Establish the structure the
chosen theorem requires.

The older Hom–Park, Teichner, and MP lanes remain resources, not
automatic restarts. Reopen one only with a concrete new geometric
mechanism or newly applicable obstruction that avoids its recorded
failure. Do not distribute the session across all old candidates.

8. PRESERVE RESULTS AND KEEP WORKING AT THE REAL GAP

Use one substantive bounded computation at a time. Save checkpoints
to durable project storage during the run, not only to /tmp afterward.

Save the selected pair, mutation certificate, marked tangles, exact
movies, identification evidence, and scoped failures. Separate
mathematical proofs, numerical filters, and unverified conjectures.

Update the existing handoff and correction register when necessary.
Commit and push audited additions to main safely, preserving concurrent
work. Report push status truthfully.

Finish with:
the concrete new object constructed;
the status of smooth sliceness and nonribbonness for the same knot;
the exact remaining gap;
the artifact paths and commit;
and the next executable geometric action.

Start now by selecting and certifying one actual mutation pair with an
applicable nonribbon-difference certificate. Extract its marked tangles
and attempt the relative concordance to a symmetric intermediate
tangle. Do not return only another plan.
```

```text
Once the boundary is understood sufficiently to justify further work,

curves, connectors, and ambient placement rather than assuming an

If this boundary is ribbon, or this annulus mechanism is obstructed,
identify exactly which geometric choice is responsible and attempt a
modification addressing that failure.

Potential changes must be actual geometric changes to the construction,
not rewritten group words: for example, a different routed excursion,
connector, or realized handle attachment. Specify the change and rebuild

Do not assume that the unlink certificate, framing control, E=0, or

integer-slope family. Do not sweep surgery coefficients using that
```
